title: Diaphragm Metering Pump

introduction.definition: A diaphragm metering pump delivers a precise, adjustable volume per stroke: a diaphragm separates the liquid from the drive, and its stroke is set by a stroke-length adjustment and speed. In the hydraulic design modelled, a plunger moves hydraulic oil that flexes the diaphragm, so the diaphragm is evenly supported and suits higher pressures.
applications: Chemical dosing: chlorine/hypochlorite, coagulants, acids, caustic
key_points: Turndown 10:1 by stroke, more with speed
Check valves on the liquid end

classification.configuration: Hydraulically actuated diaphragm metering pump (API 675 type), simplex

introduction.summary: A metering (dosing) pump delivers a precise, adjustable volume per stroke. Here a motor turns a worm gear and eccentric that reciprocate a plunger; the plunger does not touch the chemical but pushes on hydraulic oil, which flexes a PTFE diaphragm evenly. As the diaphragm retracts, the suction ball valves open and the head fills; as it advances, they close and the discharge balls lift. Output is set by stroke length (knob) and stroke rate, typically with repeatability of the order of ±1 % — used for chemical injection, water treatment and process dosing where leakage of hazardous chemicals must be avoided.

steps.text: The motor drives a worm gear and eccentric that move the plunger back and forth.
The stroke-length knob sets how far the plunger travels — the flow adjustment.
The plunger pushes hydraulic oil, which flexes the diaphragm.
On the suction stroke the suction check valve opens and the liquid end fills.

piping: Back-pressure valve to prevent siphoning; pulsation dampener; calibration column on suction.
Fit a pressure-relief valve (integral or in the discharge line) — a positive-displacement pump will build pressure until something breaks if the discharge is blocked.
commissioning: Prime the liquid end; calibrate flow at several stroke settings.

causes: Dirty check valves, air in liquid end

video_tutorials.title: Diaphragm Metering Pump — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Diaphragm Metering Pump.
A diaphragm metering pump delivers a precise, adjustable volume per stroke: a diaphragm separates the liquid from the drive, and its stroke is set by a stroke-length adjustment and speed.
In the hydraulic design modelled, a plunger moves hydraulic oil that flexes the diaphragm, so the diaphragm is evenly supported and suits higher pressures.

Typical applications include chemical dosing: chlorine/hypochlorite, coagulants, acids, caustic; boiler and cooling-water treatment; refinery and oil-field chemical injection; alumina: flocculant and additive dosing.

video_tutorials.title: Diaphragm Metering Pump — Operation

script.narration: How the Diaphragm Metering Pump works.
The motor drives a worm gear and eccentric that move the plunger back and forth.
The stroke-length knob sets how far the plunger travels — the flow adjustment.
The plunger pushes hydraulic oil, which flexes the diaphragm.
On the suction stroke the suction check valve opens and the liquid end fills.
On the discharge stroke the diaphragm pushes the liquid out through the discharge check valve.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Diaphragm Metering Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Diaphragm Metering Pump.
Check dosing rate with the calibration column.
Replace diaphragm.
Clean/replace check valves.
Change hydraulic and gear oil.
Watch for inaccurate dosing: wrong flow. Common cause: dirty check valves, air in liquid end.
Watch for diaphragm rupture: leak detector alarm. Common cause: fatigue, over-pressure.
Watch for gas locking: no delivery. Common cause: off-gassing chemicals (hypochlorite).
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
